# Interpreting Planning Plots and Sensitivity Analyses {#sec-planning-sensitivity}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Construct one-way sensitivity analyses.
- Explain robustness of the required sample to parameter uncertainty.
:::

## The idea

A single numerical sample-size estimate hides uncertainty in assumed effect sizes, SDs, prevalence, ICC and recruitment loss. Sensitivity analysis recalculates the planning target over plausible alternative values while keeping the research objective fixed. A plot should identify the varied parameter, units, fixed assumptions and result measure.

## When and how to apply it

Sensitivity plots make substantive decisions visible; they do not justify choosing the most convenient parameter. Multivariable or scenario-based sensitivity may be needed when inputs are correlated. Where analytical approximations are unreliable, simulation-based planning and specialist review should be considered.

## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Suppose anticipated prevalence ranges from 0.20 to 0.50. At fixed precision 0.05, examine how the simple independent sample-size requirement changes.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
Never report the lowest required sample from a sensitivity plot as the final number without justification.
:::
